## Purpose
`golem-engagement` provides the event and record types for Golem achievements, death recaps, graveyard genealogy, and toast notifications. It surfaces mortality and lineage mechanics to consuming systems (screens, event feeds, persistence) without UI logic.

## Key Invariants
- Achievement records are immutable once created and bound to an exact heartbeat tick
- Death recaps freeze all three mortality clocks (economic, epistemic, stochastic) at final state
- Graveyard entries are append-only; genealogy reconstructed from parent ID references
- Toast notifications carry fixed timestamp and optional expiry duration; immutable after creation

## Public API
(Anticipated from plan scope):
- `Achievement` — milestone record with Golem ID, tick, category, and metadata
- `DeathRecap` — frozen three-clock snapshot at Golem termination
- `GraveyardEntry` — genealogical record with parent ID and lineage depth
- `Toast` — transient event with timestamp and optional expiry
- `AchievementCategory` — enum for milestone types (economic, epistemic, behavioral, etc.)
- `ToastKind` — enum for notification types (death, lineage, anomaly, etc.)

## Dependencies
Currently none. Will depend on:
- `golem-core` for `Tick` and vitality primitives
- `golem-mortality` for clock state at termination
- Optional: `golem-grimoire` for memory-coupled achievement criteria

## Implementation Notes
- All records use immutable, appendable semantics; no soft-delete or in-place updates
- Death recap must capture clock state exactly at termination tick, not computed retroactively
- Parent-child genealogy uses Golem ID references; chains reconstructed via depth-first traversal of entries
- Toast expiry is wall-clock duration, not tick-based; consuming layer handles removal
- Types should derive `Copy`/`Clone` or `Serialize`/`Deserialize` for persistence and IPC

## Test Requirements
- Immutability: achievement records fail to compile if mutation is attempted
- Tick ordering: achievements from the same Golem maintain tick-monotonic order
- Genealogy reconstruction: parent-child chains correctly traversed from graveyard entry set
- Death recap snapshot: clock state at creation matches final Golem vitality state
- Toast lifecycle: expiry duration logic validates and applies correctly

## Do Not
- Don't implement achievement unlock rules in this crate; that belongs in domain layers (mortality, grimoire, context)
- Don't encode UI rendering (colors, layouts, screen bindings) in record types
- Don't use mutable genealogy structures; reconstruct chains from immutable entries
- Don't tie toast expiry to heartbeat ticks; expiry is wall-clock time, not tick-based
